newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Plains fed cattle sales light $63 - feedlots.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Plains fed cattle sales light $63 - feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains cattle near midday on Wednesday sold at $63.00 in thin volume, steady with active sales on Tuesday, feedlot sources said.

About 2,000 head sold in the Texas Panhandle and western Oklahoma area, which brought weekly movement near 73,500, they said. Kansas sales were about 600 head, which brought week to date movement near 76,000, the sources said.

Buying was light as packers appear to have more than adequate live inventory for near-term needs, especially following large purchases last week that established a weekly large movement in Kansas, they said.
Fed cattle prices the past three weeks have dropped $4.00 amid increased supplies of market-ready cattle, which have forced packers to lower beef prices to move beef inventories, the sources said.

Fabricated beef movement last week at 1,654 loads was the second largest of the year, but heavyweight choice beef (700-850 lbs) also fell $2.33 to end the week at $101.19, USDA statistics showed. Beef prices at midday were quoted down $0.48 to $1.02 per cwt, with 353 fabricated beef loads sold. Heavier-weight choice beef was quoted at $98.61, down $1.02 from Tuesday and down $2.58 from Friday.
